title: SO-F-09.3 Finding model for organisational intelligence: a finding is a graph claim capped at theory by evidence, promoted to fact only by a person or a verification, with dismissal, correction and adjudication events and no disclosure beyond the reader's permissions
request: Version 3 of this spec, which supersedes SO-F-09.2 (signed as contract k-so-f-09-2-finding-model--e25d9e; the SO-F-09.2 spec file is unchanged and stays on record, and the manifest and RECONCILIATION mark it superseded by this spec). Reason: owner delegation, 1 Nov 2026: SO-F-09.2 makes the credential-bound entry point Graph.bindFindingEvent set 'by' from the resolved credential, but raw Graph.applyOp and the replay of the op log still take data.by as written, so a forged by on a record that went around the entry point counts as the subject it names; pull request #362 (merged) records this as open work that must close before any writer calls bindFindingEvent. Base: the record base is b5932d3, the parent of the merge of #362 (5903c27). All seven files that #362 changed (changelog.d/SO-F-09.md, docs/DESIGN.md, docs/MODULES.md, docs/ORGANISATIONAL-INTELLIGENCE.md, src/engine/graph.mjs, src/engine/identity.mjs, test/findings.test.mjs) are in the scope of this spec. How each check is red: the red-green verifier copies the head's test file and the test helpers into a worktree of the base and runs the criterion's command there, so the tests run at b5932d3 and must fail by assertion, not by a load error: each test imports src/engine/graph.mjs, src/engine/identity.mjs and src/engine/oplog.mjs as namespaces and asserts that each export it uses exists. Red at b5932d3 does not by itself prove the 09.3 delta, because the finding model is not there: so the D5 tests are also run at 5903c27, the merge of #362, and must fail there by assertion on the behaviour each criterion names (a forged by applied, a scope not held, a ts not checked), which is the check that the delta, and not the missing finding model, is what is red. On main after #362 the carried criteria D3c (SO-F-09.2 D3c) and D5 (SO-F-09.2 D5, the authority table) already pass and stay green, and so do the other carried test criteria, since #362 built them. Each new criterion says how it is red. Accepted decisions: (a) a secret-free credential descriptor on the record is the trust carrier; the log is only as trusted as its writer, because a writer that builds the descriptor from caller input defeats it, and signing the log is a separate decision that stays out of this spec; (b) the descriptor is a top-level field of the record, rec.credential, and not a field of rec.data: data stays caller input and is ignored for authority. Descriptor: one flat shape, { id, identity_scope, subject }, built from a resolved actor; it is the shape resolveActor already accepts for a verified credential. A role binding's own scope is not carried: the binding message of src/engine/agentid-bind.mjs (bindingMessage) does not sign a scope, so a scope on the descriptor would be a grant the writer asserts, which pre-empts ADR 8 and duplicates PG-W-21A; carrying a binding's scope is deferred to PG-W-21B. Scope: this spec adds src/engine/oplog.mjs and test/oplog.test.mjs; src/engine/vault.mjs and src/engine/tokens.mjs stay out of scope, so this spec builds no writer, and nothing writes a finding operation yet. Known gap, out of scope: vault.mjs (_replayGraph) restores the claims of state/graph.json without applyOp, so that snapshot is trusted as written, a finding in it included; closing it needs vault.mjs and is a separate contract. Exception: SO-F-09.2 carries stop rule 1 and the contract rule assertion_removal. Exactly one carried assertion cannot survive this spec and is replaced, not removed: test AC04 of test/findings.test.mjs (line 541 on main) pins the sentence 'must be closed before any writer calls `bindFindingEvent`' on the page, which is the open-work notice this spec closes, so criterion D5l replaces it with a check that the page says the raw path is closed. The assertion at test/findings.test.mjs line 507 (code 'exists') survives, because D5h keeps the code and changes only the text. Every other carried assertion is kept. ADR 8 (trust governance in the federated model, docs/scope-one/DECISIONS.md and docs/scope-one/design/trust-governance.md, merged by #371) is proposed and not decided. PG-W-21A (the trust record, signed) and PG-W-21B (the trust book, gate and events, not to be signed before ADR 8 is signed off) own trust records and revocation. The descriptor is only the shape resolveActor accepts today, so this spec does not decide the trust root, and the trust carrier may change when ADR 8 is decided. Conflicts: #366 (merged) changed OpLog.append, which now also builds the operation envelope (_buildEnvelope); the build starts from main with it, keeps it, and a record with a credential must still build its envelope. Carried criteria: statements verbatim; commands unpiped per red-team note. The request text of SO-F-09.2 follows unchanged. Version 2 of this spec, which supersedes SO-F-09 (signed as contract k-so-f-09-finding-model-fo-cbe213, version 2, which superseded the first signed version; the SO-F-09 spec file is unchanged and stays on record, and the manifest and RECONCILIATION mark it superseded by this spec). Reason: owner delegation, 1 Nov 2026: the lead accepted four definitions that the text of SO-F-09 leaves open (a stub session; who may write a verification record; where the 'by' field comes from; how withholding works) and they are written into the contract and pinned with criteria; the scope adds only src/engine/identity.mjs, which definition 3 needs; docs/MODULES.md and changelog.d/SO-F-09.md are already in the signed scope and are not added again. Accepted definitions: (1) A stub session is an agent subject or a raw status op: neither can promote a finding to fact, by a logged status change, an adjudication, a verification or evidence. (2) A verification record may be written by a person, operator or service subject; it takes effect only when its result is a pass, and a record from an agent or with a failed result is kept and changes nothing. (3) The 'by' field of an event is set from the resolved credential (SO-F-01), never from caller input: through the credential-bound entry point a caller-supplied 'by' is ignored, so a forged by of person:x on an adjudication or service:x on a verification makes no finding a fact, and an agent credential in the personal scope resolves to an agent subject, not to person:owner. (4) Withholding is strict: if any source of a finding is withheld from the reader, the whole statement is withheld, with the reasons and corrections in its history and every entity or owner drawn from a withheld source, and an entity or owner with no source (source null) is withheld from every partial view; the reader sees only how many sources are withheld. Provisional: who may adjudicate (a person), who may verify (a person, operator or service), who may dismiss (a person or an operator subject only, by the safe default of ADR 5 that what is ungated stays denied; an agent or a service subject cannot dismiss) and the two adjudication outcomes, confirm and reject, are provisional until the permission matrix (ADR 5, open, in docs/scope-one/DECISIONS.md) and the decision and blocker workflow (SO-A-05) are decided; they are kept in one table so that deciding them changes one place. Pull request #362 builds this contract (head fe3d7f3, stacked on #349). Every requirement, criterion and scope entry of SO-F-09 is kept. Build layer of the Scope One programme, adapted from the unsigned fold of 30 Oct 2026 (fold id SO-F-09) and validated against memev main at d1c65ef. Contracts marked with a dagger are signed in the owner's vault and are not visible in this repository; they are cited by id only. Implements the design records SO-2.04 (Cross-project intelligence: evidence-backed discovery across otherwise independent work); SO-2.01 (Organisational knowledge model: relationships between people, teams, projects, decisions, artefacts and evidence) (contracts/scope-one/specs). The decision record cites this contract by id and keeps only the gaps this one does not cover. Memev contracts that land first: SO-F-01, SO-F-02. Page: docs/ORGANISATIONAL-INTELLIGENCE.md comes from the federation architecture documentation (PR #223, branch docs/federation-architecture, not on main); until that merges, the first contract to need a page creates it with its Status section, labelled planned or architectural target, and the later ones extend it. Source in the fold: #222 section 13.6 (evidence-led and cautious; dismissal and correction) and #223 ORGANISATIONAL-INTELLIGENCE.md (evidence and authority). Settled decisions this contract follows (owner decision 31 Oct 2026, docs/scope-one/DECISIONS.md): topology is local-first and the cloud is only a relay and a backup; every supported provider stands on equal footing and no work or tier depends on one; crdt-merge is reached only through the provider boundary of src/engine/merge.mjs (docs/EXTENSION-POINTS.md) and this contract adds no merge engine to the core; tiers follow docs/PRICING.md (Free core, Personal for up to 3 computers with no per-computer add-on, higher tiers by contacting us) with no Personal trial; the git backup keeps running every few minutes (sync.interval_min). Memory authority: ADR 7 (memory and project-state authority) is proposed in PR #325 and is not decided here; this contract cites it and the local-first decision, and keeps one store under the vault with no second database. Provenance: adapted from the unsigned fold of 30 Oct 2026. Changes: (1) converted from the vault task format to the memev spec format (named tests run as red-green checks on the own test file of the contract; inline regular expression flags became the flags key; hygiene and decision verifiers became commands or doc checks). (2) removed fold-only fields and the owner-decision marker field, reworded the stop rule that named a patent, and made the text pass the leak scan. (3) The fold said the graph holds claims with status fact, theory and conjecture; src/engine/graph.mjs has five (fact, theory, conjecture, contested, refuted). The cap applies to promotion to fact; contested and refuted stand as the graph derives them. (4) Boundary with PG-10.1 WP10-01 and WP10-02 (knowledge status lattice and status fields): the lattice of a fact is owned there. This contract defines only what a finding is and its cap, and maps the cap into the lattice (at most corroborated) once it lands.

tasks.description: The intelligence layer should not become an unbounded inference engine. The graph (src/engine/graph.mjs) already holds claims with status (fact, theory, conjecture, contested, refuted) and provenance, promoted and demoted as evidence arrives. A finding is such a claim with source event links, affected entities, scope and time context and confidence, whose evidence-derived status is capped at theory; fact needs a person's event or a verification record; ordinary claims keep today's rule. Conflict detection, precision and recall and decision routing are SO-F-13. Definitions accepted 1 Nov 2026: (1) A stub session is an agent subject or a raw status op: neither can promote a finding to fact, by a logged status change, an adjudication, a verification or evidence. (2) A verification record may be written by a person, operator or service subject; it takes effect only when its result is a pass, and a record from an agent or with a failed result is kept and changes nothing. (3) The 'by' field of an event is set from the resolved credential (SO-F-01), never from caller input: through the credential-bound entry point a caller-supplied 'by' is ignored, so a forged by of person:x on an adjudication or service:x on a verification makes no finding a fact, and an agent credential in the personal scope resolves to an agent subject, not to person:owner. (4) Withholding is strict: if any source of a finding is withheld from the reader, the whole statement is withheld, with the reasons and corrections in its history and every entity or owner drawn from a withheld source, and an entity or owner with no source (source null) is withheld from every partial view; the reader sees only how many sources are withheld. Provisional: who may adjudicate (a person), who may verify (a person, operator or service), who may dismiss (a person or an operator subject only, by the safe default of ADR 5 that what is ungated stays denied; an agent or a service subject cannot dismiss) and the two adjudication outcomes, confirm and reject, are provisional until the permission matrix (ADR 5, open, in docs/scope-one/DECISIONS.md) and the decision and blocker workflow (SO-A-05) are decided; they are kept in one table so that deciding them changes one place. Definition accepted 1 Nov 2026 (5): the effective actor of a finding operation is derived from the credential descriptor of its own record, never from data.by. (i) A finding operation is a record of type claim.finding or one of FINDING_EVENTS. It carries rec.credential, a top-level field of the record next to agent and client, not a field of rec.data. data stays caller input and is ignored for authority. (ii) rec.credential is a plain, secret-free, flat descriptor with exactly the keys id, identity_scope and subject, the shape resolveActor accepts for a verified credential. Any other key (a token secret, scopes, paths, a role, a principal) makes the record not applied. A role binding's scope is not carried (deferred to PG-W-21B). (iii) Graph.bindFindingEvent returns the actor it was given as credential, next to type and data, for a writer to append. OpLog.append accepts a credential only if isResolvedActor (identity.mjs) knows it, which is a real in-process barrier: an object of the same shape is refused with a thrown error and nothing is written. It builds the descriptor from the actor and copies nothing else. credential null or undefined is the same as absent and is not persisted. The key is added only when a credential is present, so a record without one is byte for byte what it was and its hash is unchanged; the hash covers the credential when there is one. oplog.mjs does not name claim.finding, admitFinding, bindFindingEvent or FINDING_EVENTS, which stay in src/engine/graph.mjs. (iv) Graph.applyOp, and so the replay of the op log which calls it, resolves rec.credential through resolveActor as of the record: at is Date.parse(rec.ts), where rec.ts must be a string that parses to a finite number. A missing or invalid ts is refused and never defaults to the clock. The subject it resolves to is the effective by: stored as raised_by, as the history by and as the decision by, and data.by is overwritten. Replay is deterministic: it gives the same graph under any clock. (v) A finding operation with no rec.credential, with one that does not resolve, with extra keys, with a missing or invalid ts, or whose subject is revoked or expired at rec.ts changes nothing in the graph: it is not applied and leaves no history entry. It fails closed. Revocation here is the descriptor's own self-reported revoked_at and expires, as the writer saw them when it wrote the record; a revocation made later in a token store does not reach back into the log, and revocation records belong to ADR 8 and PG-W-21A. resolveActor is amended to evaluate revoked_at and expires of a subject carried by a credential of the personal scope as it already does for any other scope; resolveRequest is unchanged. Role-binding expiry is deferred with role bindings. (vi) Scope parity: applyOp and replay hold the actor's scope against the finding's scope exactly as bindFindingEvent does: a finding raised in a scope the actor does not reach is not raised; a dismissal, correction, adjudication or verification of a finding in a scope the actor does not reach changes nothing; a verification must name a source event whose scope the actor may read. A refusal changes nothing. (vii) Evidence operations: a claim or claim.retract record whose id names a finding changes the finding's evidence and status only when it carries a credential that resolves and reaches the finding's scope. Without one it is ignored, so an oppose with no credential cannot refute a finding. Ordinary claims are unchanged. A claim.status record never sets a finding's status, as before. (viii) Backdating, a clock-step guard and not a security control: OpLog.append is already per-device append-only: it writes only records of its own device (dev, when a deviceId is set), each with that device's next hybrid clock value. The ts floor of a device is the largest ts, compared by Date.parse, over the credentialed records of that device. The floor is computed lazily, on the first credentialed append for that device, by one read of the log through iterate(), which covers every segment, sealed and archived ones included, and is then cached: later appends update the cache and do not read the log again, and open() reads nothing extra, so a log with no credentialed record opens, and takes uncredentialed appends, without the scan. The cache is not persisted, so a reopened log computes the floor again on its first credentialed append. A credentialed append whose ts, the one now() append already reads once, is earlier than the floor throws an error with code clock_behind and writes nothing. That check runs before the hybrid clock ticks, so the hlc, the seq and the file are unchanged. The error carries the floor and fixed remedy text (set the clock right, or wait until it passes the floor) and nothing else: not the stamped ts, not now(), and no operation type, data or credential, so two refusals under different stepped clocks are deep-equal. A ts in the credentialed records of that device that does not parse fails closed: credentialed appends for that device throw an error with the fixed code clock_floor_invalid and fixed remedy text (repair the log, or use another device id), and the error holds no stored value; uncredentialed appends are unaffected, and an unparseable ts in the records of another device does not matter. A record without a credential is appended as before, and it never lowers or releases the floor, whatever ts it is stamped with. Wall-clock ts is never compared across devices, so a device whose clock is behind another's is not refused because of the other device's records. Records of another device are not checked and no merge or import path is built for them: src/engine/merge.mjs carries no op-log records, and the admission of #358 applies no finding operations. The limit is plain: append stamps ts itself, so this guards an honest writer against a clock that stepped back; a hand edit of the log (with a recomputed hash) defeats it, revocation is the descriptor's own self-reported revoked_at, and a fresh deviceId has no floor. The consequence is that after a clock that ran far ahead, finding operations cannot be appended until the clock passes the floor, and one read of the log is paid on the first credentialed append after each open. (ix) Trust: the descriptor is a trust carrier and is not authenticated. The op log is as trusted as its writer, and a writer that builds rec.credential from caller input defeats this definition; the writer is future work and is not built here, and it must set rec.credential from the result of bindFindingEvent. Signing or authenticating log records is a separate decision and is not in this spec. The trust carrier may change when ADR 8 is decided, and when the operation envelope of PG-04.1 (docs/OPERATION-ENVELOPE.md, its authorisation field) replaces the op-log record. The snapshot of state/graph.json is trusted as written (see the known gap). (x) Uniform refusal of a taken id: a raise through bindFindingEvent, and admitFinding, whose id is already a claim gets one refusal, the same code 'exists' and the same text '<id> is taken', whether that claim is a finding the actor may reach, a finding in a scope the actor may not reach, or an ordinary claim, and the text carries nothing of that claim but the id the caller sent. This hides the kind and the scope of the claim; it does not hide that the id is taken. Scope-qualified or server-assigned ids are a follow-up and are not in this spec. Out of scope: whether a reader who can read only some of a finding's sources may adjudicate, verify or dismiss it, that is, a partial reader deciding blind, is an ADR 5 (permission matrix) decision and stays out of this spec; nothing here changes who may decide.

criteria.statement: definition 5, ts floor per device (a clock-step guard, not a security control: append stamps ts itself, a hand edit of the log defeats it, revocation is the descriptor's own self-reported revoked_at, and a fresh deviceId has no floor): the floor of a device is the largest ts, compared by Date.parse, of its credentialed records, computed lazily on the first credentialed append for that device by one read of the log through iterate() that includes archived segments, then cached. With a log directory that holds credentialed records of device A, whose clock is ten minutes ahead, OpLog.append of device B, whose clock is ten minutes behind, accepts B's credentialed records although their ts is earlier than the last ts of A, because nothing is compared across devices. With the clock of B stepped back below B's own floor, a credentialed append throws an error with code clock_behind whose only fields besides the code are the floor and a fixed remedy message (set the clock right or wait until it passes the floor); and it writes nothing: the hlc, the seq and the file are unchanged, because the check runs before the clock ticks. Two refusals under two different stepped clocks are deep-equal, and the error holds no operation type, data, credential, stamped ts or now(). An uncredentialed record appended in the same situation is accepted and does not release the floor, so the next credentialed append is still refused; a floor held by a record in an archived segment (after archiveSealed) still refuses; after the log is closed and opened again the floor is computed again and the append is still refused; once the clock passes the floor the append is accepted. Lazy and cached: the test counts the scans of the log (a read-only counter on the log, floorScans), which is 0 after open() of a log with no credentialed record and after any number of uncredentialed appends, 1 after the first credentialed append, and still 1 after a second, and 0 again after a reopen. Fail closed: a credentialed record of device B whose stored ts does not parse (written to the log by hand with its hash recomputed) makes every credentialed append of device B throw an error with code clock_floor_invalid and a fixed remedy message that holds no stored value, writing nothing and leaving the hlc, the seq and the file unchanged; an uncredentialed append of B is accepted; an unparseable ts in the records of device A does not stop B. The test states that append writes only its own device's records, that is, it is already per device append-only. Red at b5932d3, at 5903c27 and on main after #362: nothing checks the ts, so the backdated record is accepted and the assertion that append throws fails. stop_rules: Stop and post BLOCKED when a criterion cannot pass without weakening a test, skipping a test or relaxing an assertion.
Stop and ask when the work would name a client product, a person, a server or a seat in repository text; the client names live in docs/CLIENTS.md only.
Stop when the work would add a runtime dependency, a model call, a network call at install or start, a second store for project state, or any reporting that is not opt-in and off by default.
Stop when the work would move convergence logic into the core, vendor the engine, or add a merge engine beside the provider boundary of src/engine/merge.mjs.

Stop when the work would implement a federation, replication, trust, admission or computation feature beyond the specification, schema, validator and conformance test the contract names; the product keeps the planned label on it.
If any criterion fails after the fix: STOP, report the measured result, the failing check and file:line. Do not start the next task.
If the work needs a path outside scope: STOP and ask the owner to amend the contract. Never widen scope silently.

Stop unless the D5 tests were run at 5903c27 (the merge of #362) as well as at b5932d3 and fail at 5903c27 by assertion, on the behaviour the criterion names and not on a load error, a missing export or a missing test; a D5 test that is green at 5903c27 does not test the delta.
Stop when the work would decide whether a partial reader may adjudicate, verify or dismiss a finding it cannot read in full: that is an ADR 5 decision and stays out of this spec.
Stop when the work would sign, hash-chain or encrypt log records, add a key store, or authenticate rec.credential: signing the log is a separate decision and is not in this spec.
Stop when the work needs src/engine/vault.mjs or src/engine/tokens.mjs: the writer, and the restore of state/graph.json, are not part of this spec, so ask the owner for a separate contract.
Stop when the work would carry a role binding's scope on the descriptor, decide trust records or revocation records, or compare a wall-clock ts across devices: those belong to PG-W-21B and ADR 8.

Stop when the work would change resolveRequest, the signed SO-F-01 tests, the 20 criteria carried from SO-F-09.2, or an assertion of the carried tests other than the one named as the exception in the request.
